global_style_lock: Western medieval fantasy illustrated in expressive Japanese sumi-e on warm handmade washi. Black and charcoal-gray ink washes, feathered edges, irregular dry-brush contours, layered atmospheric distance and generous unpainted paper. Distinct silhouettes for tower, village, bridge, forest, river, shop and relic. Sparse muted vermilion only for danger, rivals, seals or meaningful focus. Map, town, forge, event and UI feel drawn on the same page; compact readable annotation-like controls. Not a simple sepia filter on clean vector graphics.

grand_design.visual_dna: Western medieval fantasy as expressive Japanese sumi-e on warm washi, in one legible illustrated travel journal. Rough dry-brush charcoal ink, feathered atmospheric washes and unpainted negative space make each discovered place feel memorable. Restrained muted vermilion communicates meaningful danger, seals or rivals; do not default to old blue-green/aged-gold manuscript styling. Preserve already approved combat actor identity and oblique camera anchors.

world_direction: Expressive ink washes, dry-brush contours, negative space, and paper unify map, town, shops, events, relics and UI.
Distinct landmark silhouettes and legible stronghold/POI states matter more than decorative panels at 360–430px.
Muted vermilion is a meaningful signal (rival, danger, seal), not an all-over tint.
Existing accepted combat actor anchors retain their geometry, fixed camera, pivot, animation and readability until separately reviewed.
Gameplay and safe outdoor interaction are governed by `AGENTS.md`, accepted ADRs and `docs/gameplay-spec.md`.
Generated images remain candidates until checked in the actual game.
